evidenceSections.locator: Article 25(1) and 25(2) — legal effects of electronic signatures.
evidenceSections.supports: That an electronic signature may not be denied legal effect or admissibility solely for being electronic, and that a qualified electronic signature has the equivalent legal effect of a handwritten one.

limitations: Addresses signatures by natural and legal persons. It does not confer contracting capacity on an autonomous machine, does not establish that an agent may bind a principal, and must not be read as authorising machine-formed contracts.

limitations: Editorial recommendations for journals. They bind no publisher, do not determine whether any specific correction was handled properly, and address scholarly articles rather than arbitrary published records.
